Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the MediCore Health Systems Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss MediCore Health Systems' financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Johnathan Reyes, Chief Executive Officer; Emily Carter, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Michael Chen, Chief Medical Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; David Kim, Chief Strategy Officer; Robert Lee, Chief Information Officer; Anna Morales, Chief Human Resources Officer; and Thomas Grant, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Reyes.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the second quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, touching on our payer revenue mix stability, same-facility volume and revenue growth outlook, revenue per admission momentum, total admissions and patient days expansion, payer mix shift management, strategic priorities ahead, capital investments in modernization and growth, and progress on acquisitions and divestitures. These elements underscore our disciplined approach in a complex healthcare landscape marked by demographic shifts, reimbursement dynamics, and technological evolution.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Emily Carter to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Emily Carter:
Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. As Johnathan mentioned, we had an exceptionally strong quarter. Net revenue for the second quarter was $3.90 billion, an increase of 8% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives, and the impact of our strategic acquisitions.

Let me unpack our payer revenue mix first, which remains a cornerstone of our revenue predictability and margin profile. For the quarter ended June 30, 2024, our consolidated net patient revenue payer mix was Medicare at 37.2%, Medicaid at 21.5%, commercial insurance including Medicare Advantage at 34.8%, and self-pay and other at 6.5%. This compares to Q2 2023 levels of Medicare 35.8%, Medicaid 23.1%, commercial 34.2%, and self-pay/other 6.9%. On a trailing 12-month basis, these are Medicare 36.9%, Medicaid 22.4%, commercial 35.1%, and self-pay/other 5.6%.

Medicare contributed about $1.45 billion, up 8% year-over-year on a same-facility basis, fueled by a 4.2% rise in inpatient discharges and our case mix index reaching 1.68, above peer averages. We benefited from strong volumes in major joint replacements and heart failure cases, aided by the FY2024 IPPS 2.7% update and a 0.5% productivity adjustment. Medicare Advantage now makes up 42% of this revenue, up from 38%, aligning with CMS projections. Our Sunbelt markets in Florida and Texas, covering 55% of our 45-hospital network, saw 6% Medicare utilization growth from retiree migration, while Midwest sites grew more modestly at 2%.

Medicaid, at 21.5% or $837 million, declined 7% YoY due to redeterminations affecting over 45,000 patients, with rates per discharge dropping to $8,450. Managed Medicaid, 78% of this mix through partners like Centene and Molina, improved collections, dropping AR days to 42. Rural critical access hospitals rely heavily on this at 32% of revenue, prompting advocacy for DSH allotments.

Commercial insurance, at 34.8% or $1.36 billion, was flat YoY but grew 5% in adjusted admissions, thanks to mid-single-digit rate increases on 65% of contracts, beating peer trends. Medicare Advantage carve-outs added 2.1% RAF uplift, and urban markets like Atlanta and Dallas outperformed. Capitation deals yielded $25 million in savings, with denial rates steady at 11%.

Self-pay and other, at 6.5% or $253 million, fell 6% with expanded charity care under the No Surprises Act and our Early Intervention Program screening 85% of cases promptly. Bad debt improved to 2.8% of revenue via RPA tools from XiFin. Border facilities saw uninsured rates at 11%, met with $15 million in community investments.

We're optimizing this through Epic Revenue Cycle with 3M AI coding across 90% of beds, boosting capture by 3% and cutting denials 18%. Our Payer Contracting Center aims for 85% commercial parity by year-end, with bundled pilots in ortho and cardio. We expect Medicare to 38% in H2, Medicaid stable at 21%, commercial to 36%, supporting 250-300 bps NRPA growth and full-year EPS of $12.50-$13.00.

Building on that, our total admissions reached 252,000, up 6.4% YoY from 236,800 and 3.8% QoQ from 242,500, with adjusted admissions up 7.1% YoY and 4.2% QoQ. Patient days hit 1.62 million, up 3.2% YoY from 1.57 million but down 1.1% QoQ seasonally. ALOS rose to 6.41 days with CMI at 1.72, driven by 12% ortho/neuro growth, 9% cardiology, and 5% oncology.

Sunbelt markets surged 9.2% in admissions, boosted by acquisitions and commercial mix. Northeast/Midwest grew 2.1%, offset by redeterminations. Our AI bed management cut LOS and bottlenecks, with telehealth adding 15% pre-admits.

Revenue per admission trended at $15,420, up 4.8% YoY and 4.2% same-facility, with five-year CAGR of 3.9%. CMI rose 2.3% to 1.92 from ortho/cardio strength, robotics shortening LOS to 4.7 days. Commercial mix at 52% added $450 per case from 5.2% rate wins. Sunbelt RPA hit $16,750, up 6.1%; Midwest $14,200, up 2.9%. Epic rollout improved capture 7%, AI coding added $12 million. Bundles stabilize at $28,000 episodes.

Payer mix shifts broader saw Medicare to 46% from 42%, Medicaid to 22% from 19%, commercial to 28% from 33%. Medicare FFS up 3.1% IPPS, MA at 40% reimbursing 105-110% rates but with denial rises. Medicaid stabilized via ACOs cutting readmits 7%. Commercial renegotiations yielded 4.2% hikes. Shifts cut NRPA 1.8% or $250, but CMI offset for 3.5% growth.

For same-facility outlook, Q3 volumes project 2.5-3.5% inpatient admissions, 5-7% outpatient, 1.5-2.5% ER. FY2025: 3-4% inpatient, 6-8% outpatient, 3.5-4.5% adjusted. Revenue Q3 4.5-5.5%, FY2025 5.5-6.5% with 1-2% NRPA. Southeast outperforms at +4%, AI cuts LOS 0.3 days, CAR-T ramps oncology.

Capex was $178 million in Q2, up 18% YoY, half-year $342 million toward $650-700 million FY guidance. Modernization $110 million: Epic AI $42 million, imaging $28 million, robotics $22 million, sustainability $18 million yielding 22-25% IRR. Expansion $68 million: 120-bed Florida tower, Texas ASC JV. Sunbelt focus, ROIC 15-18%.

On M&A, $425 million Gulf Coast ASCs closing Q4 adds $120 million revenue at 22% margins, $35 million synergies. $180 million Atlanta hospitals Q1 2025 accretive $0.15 EPS. Planned $600-800 million including $250 million psych facilities. Divestitures: $95 million rural sales done, $150 million pending, cutting rural to 15%.

Our operating expenses were $3.20 billion, representing 82% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in revenue cycle and supply chain. Net income for the quarter was $285 million, or $2.85 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and are raising our guidance for the full year to revenue $11.2-$11.4 billion, EBITDA $1.65-$1.75 billion, EPS $12.75-$13.25.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Chen for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Michael Chen:
Thank you, Emily. Good morning. We are making significant strides in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our integrated care coordination program has shown remarkable results, with a 25% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform, remote patient monitoring programs, and AI-powered diagnostic tools.

Following that, Lisa Patel will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including lean process redesign in the ED and supply chain automation, which have resulted in significant cost savings, improved patient flow, and enhanced staff productivity.

Next, David Kim will discuss our strategic initiatives.

David Kim:
Thank you, Lisa. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network, developing new partnerships, and investing in innovative technologies. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key markets, enhance our service offerings, and diversify our revenue streams. This includes accelerating ASC development, digital transformation with AI and Epic enhancements, payer optimization through value-based models, workforce investments, and resilience measures—targeting mid-single-digit growth and 18% EBITDA margins.

After that, Robert Lee will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

Robert Lee:
Thank you, David. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures to enhance our cybersecurity posture, ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, and mitigate the risk of data breaches. We are also investing in cloud-based solutions to improve scalability and flexibility.

Following that, Anna Morales will discuss our efforts related to workforce development and employee engagement.

Anna Morales:
Thank you, Robert. We are committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly skilled and engaged workforce. We are implementing several initiatives to improve employee satisfaction, enhance training and development opportunities, and promote a culture of diversity and inclusion, including premium shift incentives and RN academies.

Finally, Thomas Grant will elaborate on our compliance efforts.

Thomas Grant:
Thank you, Anna. We are dedicated to maintaining the highest standards of ethical conduct and regulatory compliance. We have implemented a comprehensive compliance program to ensure adherence to all applicable laws and regulations, protect patient privacy, and prevent fraud and abuse.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Johnathan Reyes.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Alex Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Thompson:
Good morning. Can you provide more details on the specific initiatives you are implementing to improve employee satisfaction and retention?

Anna Morales:
Good morning, Alex. Absolutely. Our MediCore Rewards program offers 15% premium pay for challenging shifts and travel contracts through AMN partnerships. We've launched academies in key markets to add 2,500 RNs by year-end, cutting agency reliance to under 8%. These have stabilized labor costs at 52% of revenue and boosted engagement scores by 20%, with 40% travel nurse conversions to full-time roles.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
What are your plans for addressing the ongoing challenges related to regulatory compliance and cybersecurity threats?

Thomas Grant:
Thanks, Maria. Our program includes AI-powered prior auth tools targeting 20% denial reductions and full Epic interoperability for compliance tracking. We've enhanced cybersecurity with Nuance bots and cloud migrations, ensuring HIPAA adherence and mitigating MA gridlock, positioning us ahead of peers amid rising threats.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Patel:
Can you elaborate on the potential impact of your strategic acquisitions on your long-term growth prospects?

David Kim:
Hi David. The Gulf Coast ASCs will add $120 million revenue at 22% margins with $35 million synergies, driving 8-10% of 2025 growth. Atlanta tuck-ins and psych expansions diversify high-acuity lines, with ROIC over 12% and leverage at 3.2x, fueling mid-single-digit expansion like HCA's playbook.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim:
How are you leveraging AI to improve diagnostic accuracy?

Dr. Michael Chen:
Good question, Sarah. Our Epic-Cerner AI analytics detect sepsis and readmission risks early, cutting documentation 30% and LOS 0.5 days. 3T MRIs and spectral CTs boost oncology/stroke precision, with Nuance ambient scribing freeing clinicians—yielding 10-15% outcome gains akin to peer Epic successes.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Evans with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Chris Evans:
Can you expand on Q3 same-facility guidance risks, especially payer shifts?

Emily Carter:
Thanks, Chris. We're guiding 4.5-5.5% revenue growth with stable mix, but monitoring MA denials and redeterminations. ACO expansions and AI revenue cycle offset with $50 million recaptures; derisked for 12-13% EBITDA margins.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the MediCore Health Systems Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
